title: Spotify podcast memberships let you support your favorite shows and get added perks
snippet: Spotify may not be a dedicated podcast platform, but it is launching a big new feature in podcast memberships that let you support your favorite shows in exchange for added perks. more…
fullText:
Spotify may not be a dedicated podcast platform, but it is launching a big new feature in podcast memberships that let you support your favorite shows in exchange for added perks.

Available starting today, Spotify podcast memberships work similarly to Patreon and other membership programs. Hosts can create support tiers with a monthly fee that deliver perks to their audience and, in turn, support the show. 

Spotify says examples of what creators can provide in these memberships include “exclusive audio or video, bonus episodes, fewer ads, early access, access to a show’s archive” and more. Multiple tiers can be created and pricing is customizable. 

Shows launching membership programs today include The Adam Friedland Show, Making Sense with Sam Harris, The Shawn Ryan Show, The Sculpt Society, Two Hot Takes, and 12 shows across the YMH Studios network.

	

Creators keep 90% of the revenue generated by memberships.

Spotify podcast memberships are available in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hong Kong, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the UK, and the US to start.

title: Apple announces special event for October 28: ‘Pro and tell’
snippet: Apple today announced its second experience of the month, taking place next Wednesday, October 28 at 10 a.m. PT. The tagline for this event is: “Pro and tell.” Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple today announced its second experience of the month, taking place next Wednesday, October 28 at 10 a.m. PT. The tagline for this event is: “Pro and tell.” Here’s what to expect.

This marks Apple’s second event of the month, following the “Welcome home” product launch on October 13 in New York City. That event included the debut of the new HomeView smart display, the HomePod mini 2, and a new Apple TV 4K.

Apple’s October 28 event will take place in Los Angeles. You can see the invite artwork above, which was sent to members of the press and posted on social media by Greg Joswiak.

Rumors say Apple has a slew of new products to announce at its next event, headlined by its first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and OLED. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, here’s what’s on the docket:

New 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro models with OLED displays. They will also have a Dynamic Island for the first time and will be “significantly lighter” than the current models. The new MacBook Pro models are expected to be powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

A revamped iPad mini with an OLED screen, a “revamped speaker system,” and a relocated FaceTime camera

New iMac and entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro models powered by the M6 chip, which will “look like their current versions.”

What are you most excited to see at Apple’s October 28 event? Are you planning to buy anything? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Moto Tag 2 is no longer $19.99 as the UWB tracker gears up for Pixel Tag competition
snippet: The Moto Tag 2 was always supposed to be $30, but a long-running introductory discount left the Find Hub tracker cheaper. Now, that deal has ended. more…
fullText:
The Moto Tag 2 was always supposed to be $30, but a long-running introductory discount left the Find Hub tracker cheaper. Now, that deal has ended.

Moto Tag 2 is inarguably the most capable tracker for Android’s Find Hub network thanks in no small part to its inclusion of UWB. On top of Bluetooth pings for general location, the tracker also lets you pinpoint its exact location when you get up close.

That’s why its $20 introductory price was so attractive.

The discount brought its price below virtually every other Android Find Hub tracker on the market despite the added hardware. But that price has now vanished from both Motorola’s website and from Amazon, where Moto Tag 2 is now sold for $29.99. A 4-pack costs $100, but Amazon is still selling it for less.

	

Moto Tag 2 at Motorola.com

Moto Tag 2 at Amazon

Moto Tag 2 (4-pack) at Amazon

It’s still a good value at that price – especially the 4-pack deal at Amazon – but the $10 hike certainly stings for anyone who waiting too long to score the initial price point. Even at $30, though, Moto Tag 2 remains a great value. Comparable trackers from Pebblebee and Chipolo are sold for $35 or even $40, and those don’t even have UWB. You will still need some sort of add-on if you want to mount the Moto Tag 2 to a keychain or backpack, though, as the AirTag-like form factor lacks any built-in mounting points.

Meanwhile, there’s finally another UWB tracker on the horizon in Google’s Pixel Tag. The oblong tracker was announced back in August and is set to go on sale for the same $29.99 as the Moto Tag 2 was always supposed to sell for. It’s entirely possible that Motorola will drop that price again by the time Google launches its option, but these two are currently set to battle at the same price point.
